## Facts and statements

- [statement] NIST states that the initial EWMA plays an important role in subsequent EWMA values. (low confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section4/pmc431.htm · keywords: Exponentially weighted baselines for streaming probability forecasts
- [statement] Stanford authors describe an EWMA as recursively computable without storing all past values, with per-step effort that does not grow over time. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08136v2 · keywords: Exponentially weighted baselines for streaming probability forecasts
- [statement] For a general exponentially weighted moving model, the Stanford authors state that an exact simple recursion need not be available. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08136v2 · keywords: Exponentially weighted baselines for streaming probability forecasts
- [statement] NIST defines single exponential smoothing recursively as S_t = α y_(t−1) + (1−α) S_(t−1), for 0 < α ≤ 1 and t ≥ 3. (low confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section4/pmc431.htm · keywords: Exponentially weighted baselines for streaming probability forecasts
- [statement] NIST describes exponential smoothing as weighting past observations with exponentially decreasing weights for forecasting. (low confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section4/pmc431.htm · keywords: Exponentially weighted baselines for streaming probability forecasts
- [statement] NIST states that selection of the initial EWMA becomes more important as the smoothing parameter α decreases. (low confidence) — https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section4/pmc431.htm · keywords: Exponentially weighted baselines for streaming probability forecasts
- [statement] The Stanford authors describe the half-life of their exponentially weighted model as the number of periods over which a weight decays to one-half. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08136v2 · keywords: Exponentially weighted baselines for streaming probability forecasts
